See docs/research/ballistics.md (values from search extracts of the cited pages).
Tracer: mass and burn-out distance published; drag and penetration are game values. See docs/research/ballistics.md (values from search extracts of the cited pages).

RGD-5 hand grenade: about 310 g, 110 g TNT, UZRGM fuse 3.2-4.2 s, some hundreds of light fragments. The search tool declined these look-ups in the research session; values are from general published references as remembered and must be verified against a public source. Game abstraction.
One fragment of the munition (game abstraction: all fragments equal). Drag of a rough sphere; penetration is a game value.

VOG-25 round for the GP-25/GP-30 under-barrel launcher: about 250 g, 48 g filling, about 76 m/s, arms after 10-40 m. The search tool declined these look-ups in the research session; values are from general published references as remembered and must be verified against a public source. Game abstraction.

VOG-30 30 mm grenade of the AGS-30 (M7.6d): round 0.35 kg (projectile about 0.275 kg), 185 m/s, sight range 1700 m (Wikipedia, FSVTS, Army Recognition, Arcus for the VOG-17M: search extracts, medium); kill area 112 m2 against the VOG-17M's 71 m2 (about 6-7 m lethal radius; low-medium). Game values (low): 36 g filling (the VOG-17M has 32-34 g; the VOG-30 is said to be stronger), 400 fragments of the VOG-25's kind (lab-fitted to the lethal radius), drag (fitted so the greatest range is about 1700 m), arming after 0.15 s. No delivery block: it is fired only from the AGS.
One fragment of the munition (game abstraction: all fragments equal). Drag of a rough sphere; penetration is a game value.

7.62 mm x 54 R light ball with mild-steel core (57-N-323S class): 9.6 g. Drag fitted to typical published velocities (825 -> about 600 m/s at 300 m). Penetration is a game value somewhat above the lead-core NATO ball. Penetration re-anchored after review (2026-11-11): the first values made 7.62 mm weaker against cover than 5.56/5.45 mm at every range, which is wrong; it is now set somewhat above the small calibres (more with the steel core), as a game value without a measured anchor.

7.62 mm x 54 R tracer (T-46 class) for belts, every fifth round. Derived from the ball round. Game abstraction. Penetration re-anchored after review (2026-11-11): the first values made 7.62 mm weaker against cover than 5.56/5.45 mm at every range, which is wrong; it is now set somewhat above the small calibres (more with the steel core), as a game value without a measured anchor.

82 mm HE mortar bomb (VO-832DU type, fired by the 2B14 Podnos): 3.1 kg, about 400 g TNT (manufacturer listings, search extracts); 400-600 fragments for an 82 mm HE shell (2B9 article). Fragment velocity is a game value.
One fragment of the 82 mm bomb (game abstraction: all fragments equal; mass = about the casing over the fragment count).
Smoke mortar bomb: a counted round of the mortar section's stock (rule 9); its cloud is in the faction's fireSupport (game values).

Penetration 50 mm RHA (line of sight) at 1500 m x rhaToMildSteel 1.25 = 62.5 mm mild-steel equivalent at the speed the drag model gives at 1500 m (844 m/s). Masses and drag are game values. 3UOF8 HE-I for the 2A42: muzzle velocity 960 m/s, projectile 389 g (published); filling 49 g, fragments and arming are game values (low). Bursts on a man it strikes (owner Q18). 81 mm 3D6 smoke grenade for the BMP-2's 902V dischargers (ordinary smoke; game values). The search tool cannot open pages in this container: values from published references as remembered (search extracts only).

PG-7VL (search extracts, pages not opened): 93 mm, round 2.59-2.6 kg (grenade 2.2 kg, booster 0.39 kg), muzzle 112-115 m/s, the motor ignites about 11 m out and brings it to about 300 m/s, 0.73 kg OKFOL filling; penetration 500 mm RHA (manufacturer; other sources up to 600 mm): 500 x 1.25 = 625 mm mild-steel equivalent; effective range 300 m against a vehicle. Game values (low): motor 0.1 s after launch for 0.5 s at 370 m/s2, drag, self-destruct 4.5 s (the 920 m figure belongs to the OG-7V), dispersion 1.5 mrad, 3 s to aim, danger zone 30 m behind, 120 fragments of its body, 20 fragments thrown inside a hull it penetrates.

RPO-A Shmel thermobaric rocket (M7.6d): the whole disposable tube 11 kg (Wikipedia/Jane's; Modern Firearms 12 kg), 2.1 kg thermobaric filling, minimum range 20 m, effective 200 m, sight 600 m (search extracts, medium); much stronger in enclosed spaces than in the open (Euro-SD, medium; the TNT-equivalent claims are contested and not used). Game values (low): the round 3 kg, 125 m/s, drag, dispersion 2.5 mrad, 3 s to aim, 15 m danger zone behind, 40 case fragments, self-destruct after 8 s; in the open the plain blast of its 2.1 kg (severe within about 3.8 m); bursting in a room or on its outer wall it fills that room: every man in it takes the blast at 1.6 x the radii, no wall shielding him (an abstract effect, SPEC 3). No launcher item: the round is the tube (disposable); fired only at men and positions, never at a vehicle (role antiPersonnel).

9M113M Konkurs-M, the in-service missile of the BMP-2's 9P135M launcher (which also fires the 9M113 and the 9M111 Fagot); search extracts only, pages not opened. Published (sources agree): range 75-4000 m (wire), semi-automatic command to line of sight by wire, tandem shaped charge 750-800 mm RHA behind reactive armour (the 9M113 600 mm): 750 x 1.25 = 937 mm mild-steel equivalent. Speed: about 208 m/s (Wikipedia; other sources 200-300 m/s), i.e. about 19-20 s to 4000 m. Missile mass 14.6 kg (9M113) to 16.5 kg (BDL, Konkurs-M): 16.5 used; launch container about 10 kg more (game value). Game values (low): leaves the tube at 80 m/s (the launcher's velocity) and speeds up at 65 m/s2 to 208 m/s, turns at most 12 deg/s, gunner's tracking error 0.3 mrad (skill 0.5) wandering over about 1 s, aims 0.4 s ahead along the sight line, filling 1.8 kg (warhead about 2.7 kg), 150 fragments, arms after 0.5 s, destroys itself after 21 s (end of the wire); guidance lost: thrown off by about 60 mrad and falls. A simple model (owner 2026-11-13); full guided-weapon modelling is M9.

RDG-2 smoke hand grenade: about 500 g, 60-90 s of intensive smoke, a screen up to about 30 m long and 5-8 m wide (search extracts; the RDG-2M about 600 g, 50-70 s, 50 x 10 m). Game abstraction: a round cloud of 10 m radius (about the screen's area, no wind drift) for 75 s, smoking 2 s after the throw (low).

120 mm OF-843B high-explosive mortar bomb (M8.3a, for the 2B11): about 16 kg (search extracts); filling 1.4 kg and 1,500 fragments are game values in line with the German 120 mm round. A counted round (rule 9).
Fragment of the 120 mm mortar bomb (M8.3a): as the 82 mm bomb's (game value).
120 mm smoke mortar bomb (M8.3a, for the 2B11): a counted round; its cloud is the faction's fireSupport smoke (game values).

152 mm HE-FRAG shell 3OF45 for the 2S19 Msta-S (M8.4): 43.56 kg (FAS, search extract); about 6.9-7.6 kg of explosive (one less reliable guide: 6.86 kg TNT); 7.6 kg and 3,000 fragments are game values, low.
Fragment of the heavy artillery shell (M8.4): heavier than a mortar bomb's (game value, low).
Heavy artillery smoke shell (M8.4): a counted round; its cloud is the faction's artillery smoke (game values, low).

Heavy artillery illumination shell (M8.4; M485A2 class): a parachute flare of about 1,000,000 cd burning up to 120 s, sinking 4-5 m/s (FAS / Yugoimport extracts); ejected about 600 m up (game value). Saved in the state; its light on the ground: M9.6 (core/spotting.json night.flare*).

Mortar illumination bomb (M8.4): parachute flare; candela, burn, height and descent are game values in the range of public mortar illumination rounds (none reached). Saved in the state; its light on the ground: M9.6 (core/spotting.json night.flare*).

9M131 missile of the 9K115-2 Metis-M (M9.3b, owner: the Russian dismounted missile is a Metis-M team at company level); search extracts only, pages not opened. Published: 130 mm, 13.8 kg in its launch tube (13 kg bare round in some sources), range 80-1500 m (Metis-M; the Metis-M1 80-2000 m: 2000 used, owner's plan), semi-automatic command to line of sight by wire, average speed about 200 m/s (FAS gives 287 m/s, 8 s to the maximum range: not used), tandem shaped charge about 800 mm RHA behind reactive armour (Metis-M1 900-980): 800 x 1.25 = 1000 mm mild-steel equivalent. Game values (low): bare missile 11 kg, leaves the tube at 80 m/s and speeds up at 80 m/s2 to 200 m/s, turns at most 14 deg/s, gunner's tracking error 0.35 mrad (skill 0.5; a tripod sight, a little worse than the BMP-2's), filling 1.6 kg, 120 fragments, arms after 0.5 s, destroys itself after 13 s (end of the wire at about 2000 m); guidance lost: thrown off by about 60 mrad. No `delivery` block: it is not a shoulder-fired round (the team's tripod fires it, systems/missile-team.ts).

3BM60 Svinets-2 APFSDS (depleted uranium) for the 125 mm 2A46M-5; needs the new autoloader (published). Search extracts only (pages not opened in this container). Penetration (low): the maker's 300 mm at 60 degrees at 2 km (about 600 mm line of sight), Wikipedia 640-700 mm at 0 degrees: 620 mm RHA at 2000 m x 1.25 = 775 mm mild steel at the speed the drag model gives there (1586 m/s from 1660 m/s, game drag a 0.40). Masses and drag are game values; long rod behaviour as the 120 mm DM63A1. cartridgeMassKg here is the projectile alone (the round item's charge); the case and propellant are the item's own mass (M7.6a review fix).

3BM42 Mango APFSDS, the round that fits the T-72's old carousel (published). Search extracts only (pages not opened in this container). Penetration (low): 450-500 mm RHA at 0 degrees at 2 km in published tables: 460 mm x 1.25 = 575 mm mild steel at the speed the drag model gives at 2000 m (1583 m/s from 1700 m/s; a thicker two-piece rod, d 0.03 m). Masses and drag are game values. cartridgeMassKg here is the projectile alone (the round item's charge); the case and propellant are the item's own mass (M7.6a review fix).

3OF26 HE-FRAG for the 125 mm gun. The search for it was refused; projectile about 23 kg, about 3.4 kg filling, about 850 m/s are from memory, not from a source (low). Fragments are the 120 mm mortar bomb's (game abstraction); count and speed are game values. The T-90M's programmable 3VOF128 Telnik is not modelled. cartridgeMassKg here is the projectile alone (the round item's charge); the case and propellant are the item's own mass (M7.6a review fix).

Balance pass 6 (owner Q8, 2026-11-20: 'Yes, low confidence'): the 3OF26 high-explosive round with the 3VM-12 electronic time fuze of the Ainet remote-detonation system, as the T-90M's fire control (Kalina) is said to set it from the laser range; only the T-90M feeds it, the T-72B3M keeps the impact-fuzed 3OF26. Modelled as the Leopard's DM11: aimed 3 m over the point and timed at the muzzle, it bursts over it and throws the 3OF26's fragments all round; point detonation stays the setting at a hull or a house. Every figure is the 3OF26's (from memory, low) and the burst height is a game value. Whether line T-90M carry Ainet rounds, or the 3VOF128 Telnik rounds with ready-made fragments, and in what numbers, is not known from open sources (search extracts and memory only; pages cannot be opened in this container): low. cartridgeMassKg here is the projectile alone (the round item's charge).

9M119M Refleks-M, fired through the 125 mm gun's bore (published): laser beam-riding, 75-5000 m (100 m minimum here), missile 17.2 kg, tandem shaped charge 700-750 mm RHA (650-700 behind reactive armour): 700 x 1.25 = 875 mm mild steel. Search extracts only (pages not opened in this container). Game values (low): leaves the bore at 280 m/s and cruises at 300 m/s (about 17 s to 5000 m), turn rate, tracking error, filling 2.0 kg, 150 fragments, arming after 0.3 s, self-destruct at 20 s; the round with its case 24.3 kg. cartridgeMassKg here is the projectile alone (the round item's charge); the case and propellant are the item's own mass (M7.6a review fix).
